newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: ARCON half-yr pre-tax profit 36,000 punts.
newsitem.headline: ARCON half-yr pre-tax profit 36,000 punts.

text.p: ARCON International Resources Plc said on Wednesday that it made a pre-tax profit of 36,000 Irish pounds in the half year to February 1997 compared with a loss of 145,000 punts in the same period last year.
Turnover in the first half rose to 933,000 Irish pounds from 746,000 in the same period of 1996, due mainly to higher oil prices, ARCON said in a statement.
Earnings per share were 0.01 Irish pence against a loss of 0.05 pence last time.

As concentrate sales from its lead-zinc mine at Galmoy in the Irish midlands did not commence until March 1997, the result does not take into account the successful commencement of operations at Galmoy, the company said.
ARCON said it is now focusing on optimising its production rates at the Galmoy mine as the construction works are nearly complete.
The company said it was very well placed to take advantage of the high zinc price and the strong dollar and was also very pleased with the results from its exploration programme.
A two-year 1.5 million punt exploration programme around the mine and the Galmoy district is being continued to September 1998.

ARCON said its hydrocarbon production assets continued to perform well in the first half with its interest in the producing Claymore and Singleton fields and buoyant oil prices helping to generate good cashflow.
Progress continues with the evaluation of production feasibility on the Helvick oil field and the Ardmore gas field, it said.

"With strong cashflow from our mining operations and continued exploration success, ARCON will be seeking new investment opportunities that will add to its asset base and spread of activities," chairman Brendan Gilmore said.
